root_cause.text: The svm_set_nested_state() function incorrectly used a WARN_ON_ONCE for a failure of nested_svm_load_cr3(), which can be easily triggered by userspace by setting a CR3 value that is invalid given the current guest CPUID (e.g., modifying max physical address bits after loading CR3), leading to a user-controllable kernel warning.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE description and patch commit message explicitly show that modifying CPUID after loading CR3 (e.g., setting CR3 with bit 44 and then reducing max_phys_addr to 36) triggers the WARN at arch/x86/kvm/svm/nested.c:1877. The patch removes the `WARN_ON_ONCE(ret)` and simply returns the error, confirming that the failure condition is reachable from userspace.

Continuation of the nested_svm_load_cr3 call; the parameters contribute to the function call that may fail due to invalid CR3.
Core vulnerable statement: uses WARN_ON_ONCE for a failure that can be easily triggered by userspace, causing a user-controllable kernel warning.
Error path executed when nested_svm_load_cr3 fails; although the goto is standard, it is part of the vulnerable code path that triggers the warning.
Statement executed after successful CR3 load; while not directly vulnerable, it is in the same function context and its execution depends on the success of the call that produces the warning.
